doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Electricity at 13, the player piano and first piano lessons
summary: No electricity until he was 13; his father learned from the player piano and Allison took lessons from age five.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you remember your grandfather at all?
No. I remember riding in his buggy.
I gather that electricity didn’t come to Tippo until you were 13.
You grew up with a wind-up Victrola, no electricity, no radio. The center of the world was the general store and the filling station. And you had a piano.
Yeah. Well, the piano was in my grandfather’s house. My father learned how to play the piano from the wind-up....
I gather he favored ragtime, and Scott Joplin and things like that.
Yeah. Well, I don’t know whether he knew about Scott Joplin. But Fats Waller, I remember...
That’s right. He did like Fats Waller.
Well, he certainly wasn’t alone in that. I gather, again from reading the interviews, that you showed an aptitude for the piano very young.
I took piano lessons when I was 5 years old. I took them for three or four years. But the teacher was...
